hypotheses.justification: The point `p` appears nowhere in the statement or conclusion. The proof only passes it to `compact_mixed_energy` and `compact_test_gradient`. Those pass it on to heat-flow lemmas such as `heat_compact_uniform_slope`, where it is only an arbitrary base point. `NoncollapsedRCD` does not force `X` to be nonempty, so `p` currently supplies nonemptiness. Without `p`, the theorem still holds. Split with `isEmpty_or_nonempty X`. If `X` is nonempty, pick `p` with `Classical.arbitrary` and run the existing proof unchanged. If `X` is empty, `hausdorff n X = 0` by `MeasureTheory.Measure.eq_zero_of_isEmpty`, since `hausdorff n X` is a scalar multiple of `Measure.hausdorffMeasure n`. So every `=ᵐ[hausdorff n X]` statement is trivially true, and the existence of `G`, `γf` and `γa` can be witnessed by `0`. Nothing else in the proof uses `p`: the density of the core comes from `regularDirichletCore_dense`, which takes no `p`, and the Koszul computation is purely algebraic. I did not check how `LocalHessianPairing` is defined, so the empty-`X` case rests on this argument rather than on a verified proof.
